increment_paragraph: **SP5-GLOBAL-PROSE-PREMISE-BAN (2026-11-22).** User decision 2026-11-20 (premises are condition symbols, not sentences); SP1-SP4 had converted every provider premise; launched 2026-11-22. The contract format refuses resource_premise(NAME, "STATEMENT") in every vocabulary and on every load route with the new diagnostic QF001 (namespace QF***, owned by the premise reader on the QI*** precedent; no Q code allocated): qcore_frontend::premise_formula::premise_clause, which the structural parser, the contract, bounds and local-condition loaders and the operator gate all share, refuses any statement that is or holds a string literal and returns only formulas (PremiseStatement removed); on the compiler route the refusal is the Q000 parse error naming QF001. This is the load-time ban for every crate, shipped or user, with no opt-in (discharging SP2-SHIPPED-PROVIDER-PROSE-BAN); a test rewrites a premise of each crate on the real load path as a string and shows elaboration and parsing refuse it; the per-crate scans and OpenSSL's checker stay. C04.21's reserved entry-snapshot premise states quant all #m in #condition_reads: #m in #entry_stable over two terms in a new SP5 vocabulary block (specification, Rust, Lean). Every test and fixture premise states a formula over registered terms (88 string matches in 31 files at base; after, 35 in 12, each a refusal case, the reader's own refusal text and vectors, a per-crate ban or the frozen compiler fixture); tests of the string form now test its refusal. Frozen texts that state prose (docs/reports .qv, the compiler fixture, SP2's byte restoration) are read only through the test-side legacy reader tests/support/legacy_prose_premise.rs, which writes each statement SP2 recorded as its formula; a test checks every file naming it is test code. The frozen guarded adoption plan, decomposition applications and symbolic-adoption inventory keep their exact byte and digest checks on the restored module and replay on the current module with the plan and graphs lifted. Provider comments describing the string form name the formula form (comment-only, recorded and reversible in comments.json; file digests resynced, no pin moved). Spec C04.18, C04.18.9, C04.21, grammar G05, rule 13h (and 14x's mention), the L21 table and the diagnostics page updated. Lean: QCore.PremiseFormula's clause acceptance (string_is_not_a_premise, formula_premise_iff_wf, accepted_is_wf, accepted_is_a_formula, accepted_denotes, clause_vectors_agree bound to the Rust CLAUSE_DECISION_VECTORS), audited. Premises stay undischarged metadata: no move predicted on any route.

ledger.why: DISCHARGED by SP5-GLOBAL-PROSE-PREMISE-BAN: the contract format refuses resource_premise(NAME, "STATEMENT") in every vocabulary and on every route with QF001 (qcore_frontend::premise_formula::premise_clause, the one reader the parser and every loader share, returns formulas only); every test and fixture premise migrated to a C04.18.9 formula over registered terms, the string-form tests now refusal tests; frozen texts read only through the test-side legacy reader tests/support/legacy_prose_premise.rs, confined to test code by a test; C04.21's reserved snapshot premise stated as a formula over a two-term SP5 block; spec C04.18, grammar G05, rule 13h updated; Lean QCore.PremiseFormula's clause acceptance (string_is_not_a_premise, accepted_is_wf, clause_vectors_agree, ...) audited; no production premise changed and no move predicted.

DISCHARGED by SP5-GLOBAL-PROSE-PREMISE-BAN: the load-time refusal is unconditional rather than opt-in: the core's one premise reader refuses a string statement (QF001) for every crate on every load path, shipped qcore-provider-* crates included; compiler/tests/contract_inherit_qcore_provider.rs a_string_premise_in_any_crate_on_the_load_path_is_refused_at_load rewrites a premise of each crate on the real load path (qcore-provider-libevent, qcore-provider-librdkafka and quirin-provider-fluent-bit required) as a string and shows elaboration and parsing refuse it; the per-crate tests stay as belt-and-braces.
